claims.text: SSH gives you a shell session on another machine, and the connection carrying it is encrypted in both directions. The far machine runs an SSH server program, which answers the client, checks the authentication and starts what was asked for.
claims.source_hint: OpenSSH ssh(1) manual, DESCRIPTION (first paragraph); sshd(8) manual, DESCRIPTION

claims.text: The two ends first agree, over the still-unprotected connection, on a shared secret that is never itself sent, and everything after that exchange is encrypted with keys derived from it.
claims.source_hint: RFC 4253 sections 7 (key exchange) and 6.3 (encryption)

claims.text: In public-key authentication the client names the user and sends the public key it will use; the server, holding that public key for the user, has the client sign a value that includes data from this session with the private key, and verifies the signature against the stored key.
claims.source_hint: RFC 4252 section 7 (Public Key Authentication Method), SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_PK_OK and the signed data

claims.text: A signature is a value the private key computes from some data; the matching public key confirms that private key made it from that data but cannot make one itself, and the private half cannot be derived from the public one. The private key is never sent over the connection.
claims.source_hint: RFC 4252 section 7; OpenSSH ssh-keygen(1) manual, DESCRIPTION

claims.text: Given no command, ssh has the server start an interactive shell with a prompt; given a command, a shell on the remote machine runs just that command line, with no prompt, and ssh finishes when it finishes.
claims.source_hint: OpenSSH ssh(1) manual, DESCRIPTION, 'If a command is specified'; sshd(8), 'the command is executed ... using the user's shell'

claims.text: A command run over SSH runs as a process on the remote machine, so its working directory and every path it opens are that machine's; its environment variables are mostly the ones that machine set, though ssh may carry a few across from the client; its output is sent back (also sections 6, 9).
claims.source_hint: OpenSSH sshd(8) manual, 'Command execution and data forwarding'; ssh_config(5) SendEnv and sshd_config(5) AcceptEnv (the 'mostly' / 'a few')

claims.text: scp and rsync copy files between machines over a connection of the same kind, rather than giving the caller a shell.
claims.source_hint: OpenSSH scp(1) manual, DESCRIPTION; rsync(1) manual, 'remote shell' transport

claims.text: At stage-0 scripts/terminal/ssh-into-lab.sh writes one ssh call across lines 6-10 (lines 6-9 end in a backslash) that connects as dev@localhost with the key file secrets/lab_key and runs 'hostname; whoami; ls -1 /repo/db' on the far side; the recorded run shows one connection.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/scripts/terminal/ssh-into-lab.sh lines 6-10 and outputs/stage-0/scripts/terminal/ssh-into-lab.txt at stage-0

claims.text: The captured output of that script at stage-0 is the five lines donhang-lab, dev, queries, schema.sql, seed.sql, in that order: the three ';'-separated quoted commands ran one after another, hostname's answer first, then whoami's, then the ls listing.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/outputs/stage-0/scripts/terminal/ssh-into-lab.txt; scripts/terminal/ssh-into-lab.sh line 10

claims.text: scripts/dev-secrets.sh creates the key pair on the learner's laptop as secrets/lab_key and secrets/lab_key.pub when secrets/lab_key is missing, and scripts/up.sh runs it before starting the lab.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/scripts/dev-secrets.sh and scripts/up.sh at stage-0

claims.text: The lab box is started with lab_key.pub as the authorised public key for user dev and with password logins turned off, so over SSH the key file is the only way in; docker compose exec still opens a shell in the container without it, which is how the other stage-0 scripts run.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/docker-compose.yml, lab service: PUBLIC_KEY_FILE, USER_NAME, PASSWORD_ACCESS; examples/don-hang/scripts/lab-run.sh

claims.text: The example folder is bind-mounted into the lab box at /repo, read-only: the box reads the laptop's folder itself when a path under /repo is opened, nothing is copied and a write is refused; so ls -1 /repo/db lists the editor's names and ls / on the box lists repo.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/docker-compose.yml, lab service volumes: ./:/repo:ro; Docker bind mounts, readonly/ro

claims.text: StrictHostKeyChecking=no and UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null together stop ssh from recording or checking which machine answered: the second points the file of recorded host keys at /dev/null, which reads as empty and discards writes. LogLevel=ERROR makes ssh print less.
claims.source_hint: OpenSSH ssh_config(5) manual, StrictHostKeyChecking, UserKnownHostsFile and LogLevel; null(4)

claims.text: hostname prints the name of the machine it runs on, whoami prints the user the process runs as, and ls -1 lists one name per line, which is why the answers name the lab box, dev and the three files of db.
claims.source_hint: hostname(1) and whoami(1) manuals, DESCRIPTION

claims.text: Turning off host checking, as two of the three -o lines do (StrictHostKeyChecking=no and UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null), is acceptable only when the machine answering is on the same laptop; against a machine reached over a network it removes the guarantee that the same server is answering.
claims.source_hint: OpenSSH ssh_config(5), StrictHostKeyChecking rationale

claims.text: Copying files to a machine you do not sit at and then running commands on them over a remote shell connection has long been a common way to put software onto that machine, and was often how it was done before tools automated it (also sections 8, 9).
claims.source_hint: No single specification; reviewer may mark unverified. Nearest documentary support: rsync(1) and scp(1) manuals describing the file-distribution use case.

claims.text: A signature the client makes covers data unique to the current session, so a recorded signature cannot be replayed to log in later.
claims.source_hint: RFC 4252 section 7, the signature blob includes the session identifier

claims.text: An SSH private key file may itself be protected with a passphrase, in which case a copy of the file alone does not let its holder log in; the lab's key is made without one (ssh-keygen -N '' in scripts/dev-secrets.sh).
claims.source_hint: OpenSSH ssh-keygen(1) manual, -N; examples/don-hang/scripts/dev-secrets.sh at stage-0

claims.text: A machine has many numbered ports and a program answering connections waits at one; localhost is the name a machine uses for itself, and the lab box publishes its SSH server on port 2222 of the Docker host, the laptop, so dev@localhost with -p 2222 reaches the box.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/docker-compose.yml, lab service: LISTEN_PORT 2222 and ports 2222:2222; Docker port publishing; hosts(5) loopback name

claims.text: In scripts/terminal/ssh-into-lab.sh at stage-0, line 1 is the interpreter line, line 3 is set -euo pipefail and line 4 is cd "$(dirname "$0")/../..", which from scripts/terminal/ lands on the example folder's root.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/scripts/terminal/ssh-into-lab.sh at stage-0, lines 1-4

claims.text: At stage-0 ssh-into-lab.sh has no line restarting it inside the lab box (the other scripts/computer and scripts/terminal scripts have [ -f /.dockerenv ] || exec lab-run.sh), so bash and ssh run on the laptop and only the quoted commands run on the box.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: scripts/terminal/tour.sh line 5; scripts/lab-run.sh last line; scripts/terminal/ssh-into-lab.sh lines 1-10

claims.text: During key exchange the server signs the exchange with the private half of its host key pair; ssh normally records the public half on the first connection to a machine and checks the signature against it later, which keeps a machine in between from making the agreement in its place.
claims.source_hint: RFC 4253 section 8 (server signs the exchange hash with its host key); OpenSSH ssh_config(5), StrictHostKeyChecking and UserKnownHostsFile; ssh(1), known_hosts

claims.text: At stage-0 docker-compose.yml also mounts ./secrets into the lab box at /keys, so the private key file is visible inside the box, although the box needs only lab_key.pub (PUBLIC_KEY_FILE) to accept the key.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/docker-compose.yml at stage-0, lab service: volumes ./secrets:/keys, PUBLIC_KEY_FILE /keys/lab_key.pub

claims.text: A web server usually proves itself to a browser by using the private key of a certificate the browser can trace, through a chain of signatures, back to a signer it already trusts.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 section 4.3.3 (refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt:1325-1330): authority from the private key of a certificate; chain of trust from a trust anchor

claims.text: Line 3 of ssh-into-lab.sh, set -euo pipefail, makes bash stop the script when a command fails and the failure is not handled.
claims.source_hint: bash(1) manual, set builtin, -e -u -o pipefail; examples/don-hang/scripts/terminal/ssh-into-lab.sh line 3 at stage-0
